routes.label: Separate exterior faces and tunnel walls

question:
In the adjoining figure, a wooden cube has edges of length \(3\) meters. Square holes of side one meter, centered in each face, are cut through to the opposite face. The edges of the holes are parallel to the edges of the cube. The entire surface area including the inside, in square meters, is

[Figure 1](figures/1982_AMC_12_Q16_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Count the remaining outside surface and the newly exposed tunnel walls separately. The three perpendicular tunnels overlap exactly in the central cube of side \(1\) meter.

Each of the original six faces has area \(3^2=9\) square meters and loses a square opening of area \(1\). Thus the remaining exterior contributes
\[
6(9-1)=48
\]
square meters.

Outside the central cube, the tunnels form six arms, one leading to each face. Centering leaves each arm with length \((3-1)/2=1\) meter. Each arm has four square walls, each \(1\) meter by \(1\) meter, so the interior area is
\[
6\cdot4\cdot1=24
\]
square meters. Both ends of each arm are open. All six faces of the central cube open into these arms, so there is no additional wall at the central crossing.

These outside faces and interior wall panels cover the entire surface, and distinct panels share at most edges, which contribute no area. The total is
\[
48+24=\boxed{72\text{ m}^2},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
Imagine dividing the original cube into \(27\) cubes of side \(1\) meter. The centered square tunnels follow this division exactly. They remove the central cube and the six cubes at the centers of the large cube's faces. The remaining cubes are precisely the eight corner cubes and the twelve cubes at the middles of its edges.

Each corner cube has three faces on the outside. Its other three faces touch the neighboring edge cubes, so it contributes exactly three exposed square faces.

Each edge-middle cube has two faces on the outside. Of its other four faces, two touch the corner cubes at the ends of that edge, and two face removed face-center cubes. Thus it contributes exactly four exposed square faces, including its two tunnel walls.

Every surface panel is an exposed face of exactly one remaining unit cube, so this counts the whole surface without duplication. Each such face has area \(1\) square meter. Therefore the surface area is
\[
8\cdot3+12\cdot4=24+48=\boxed{72\text{ m}^2},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
